instrument_candidates.name: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act)
instrument_candidates.summary: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of the European Parliament and of the Council laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence. Signed 13 June 2024 and published in the Official Journal on 12 July 2024. It entered into force on 1 August 2024. Article 113 sets staged application dates. The EUR-Lex page shows a consolidated version dated 27 July 2026, reflecting amendment by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, which moved the high-risk application dates (see eu-digital-omnibus-ai).
key_obligations: Application schedule per consolidated Article 113: prohibitions and AI literacy (Chapters I and II) from 2 February 2025; GPAI, governance and penalties provisions from 2 August 2025 (except Article 101 fines on GPAI providers, which apply from 2 August 2026); general application 2 August 2026; Annex III high-risk from 2 December 2027; Annex I high-risk from 2 August 2028; new Article 5 prohibitions added by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 from 2 December 2026
High-risk AI system requirements for Annex III systems now apply from 2 December 2027 and for Annex I systems from 2 August 2028, per the amending regulation
AI literacy (Article 4) as amended: providers and deployers must take measures to support AI literacy

timeline.note: Regulation signed (date of signature per EUR-Lex).
Published in the Official Journal of the EU (OJ L, 12.7.2024).
Entered into force on the twentieth day following publication in the OJ (Article 113).
Amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI), which entered into force on this date; EUR-Lex shows a consolidated version of this date.

instrument_candidates.name: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI)
instrument_candidates.summary: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 8 July 2026 amending Regulations (EU) 2024/1689, (EU) 2018/1139 and (EU) 2023/1230 as regards simplification of the implementation of harmonised rules on AI. Published in the Official Journal L series on 24 July 2026 and in force from the third day after publication, 27 July 2026. It defers high-risk application dates and adjusts several AI Act provisions.
key_obligations: High-risk AI systems under Annex III apply from 2 December 2027
High-risk AI systems under Annex I apply from 2 August 2028
Article 4 AI literacy changed to an obligation to take measures supporting AI literacy
Article 5 extended with prohibitions on systems generating non-consensual intimate images and child sexual abuse material, applying from 2 December 2026 (Article 113 as amended)
SMEs and small mid-cap enterprises (SMCs) may provide technical documentation in a simplified manner and get priority access to AI regulatory sandboxes
Special-category data processing for bias detection extended beyond high-risk providers under safeguards

timeline.note: Regulation dated 8 July 2026 (signature date per EUR-Lex title).
Entered into force on the third day following publication.

instrument_candidates.name: General-Purpose AI Code of Practice (EU)
instrument_candidates.summary: Voluntary code published by the European Commission on 10 July 2025 (per the Commission page). Its Transparency and Copyright chapters offer providers of general-purpose AI models a way to demonstrate compliance with Article 53 of the AI Act; the Safety and Security chapter addresses providers of models with systemic risk under Article 55. The Commission page lists 21 organisations as signing the full code and xAI signing only the Safety and Security chapter. Signing the code is voluntary.
key_obligations: Transparency chapter: supports demonstrating Article 53 compliance
Copyright chapter: supports demonstrating Article 53 compliance
Safety and Security chapter: for providers of systemic-risk models (Article 55)

instrument_candidates.name: Switzerland: Federal Council approach to AI regulation (ratification of Council of Europe AI Convention)
instrument_candidates.summary: On 12 February 2025 the Federal Council decided that Switzerland intends to ratify the Council of Europe Convention on AI and make the necessary amendments to Swiss law, while continuing sector-specific AI regulation. The Federal Chancellery page states a bill to be prepared by the FDJP with DETEC, the FDFA and other federal offices and submitted for consultation is due by end of 2026, along with a plan for non-binding measures, and that the Federal Chancellery has maintained an AI contact point for the Federal Administration since 1 February 2026. According to the Federal Chancellery, there is not yet any overarching legislation in Switzerland that deals specifically with AI.
key_obligations: Planned implementing bill to cover transparency, data protection, non-discrimination and supervision; consultation draft due by end of 2026 (bk.admin.ch)
Continued work on AI regulation in specific sectors such as healthcare and transport (Federal Council, 12 February 2025)
Non-binding measures (industry solutions, voluntary commitments) planned

timeline.note: Federal Council decides to ratify the Council of Europe AI Convention and amend Swiss law.
Federal Chancellery contact point on AI for the Federal Administration in operation; consultation bill (FDJP with DETEC and FDFA) and non-binding measures plan due by end of 2026.
